text: How many ciprofloxacin studies are there for Escherichai coli?

Abstract  
Bacterial transcriptomic studies under antibiotic stress inform mechanisms of resistance and adaptation. We quantified the number of publicly available Escherichia coli gene expression series involving ciprofloxacin exposure. Using NCBI’s GEO database via the Entrez E-utilities esearch endpoint, we applied filters: organism “Escherichia coli”, free-text term “ciprofloxacin”, and entry_type “gse”. We retrieved a total_count of 37 Series (GSE) records matching these criteria [1]. No additional literature records were retrieved. This count reflects the total ciprofloxacin-related expression profiling studies in GEO as of the query date. Knowing the availability of such data can guide meta-analyses of antibiotic response and highlight resource gaps. Future work may expand to include other antibiotic classes, broader array platforms, or integrate data from RNA-seq and microarray to assess cross-study reproducibility.

I. Introduction  
Background. Ciprofloxacin is a commonly used fluoroquinolone antibiotic whose effects on Escherichia coli gene expression have been studied using high-throughput techniques. Public repositories like GEO hold these transcriptomic data.  
Literature Review. No literature was retrieved for this query.  
Knowledge Gap. The number of GEO studies specifically profiling E. coli under ciprofloxacin treatment has not been summarized.  
Objective & Hypothesis. We aimed to determine the total number of ciprofloxacin‐related expression profiling studies in GEO for E. coli, hypothesizing that multiple such Series exist but their count is unknown.

II. Materials and Methods  
Study Design. We queried GEO via the Entrez E-utilities to identify Series (GSE) matching ciprofloxacin exposure in E. coli.  
Materials. NCBI GEO database accessed through the geo_search tool.  
Procedures. We invoked geo_search with parameters:  
• organism="Escherichia coli"  
• term="ciprofloxacin"  
• entry_type="gse"  
• max_results=10  
The tool returned metadata including total_count.  
Statistical Analysis. The total_count field (37) was taken as the number of matching studies. No deduplication was required.

III. Results  
Findings. The query returned a total_count of 37 ciprofloxacin‐related Escherichia coli Series in GEO.

IV. Discussion  
Interpretation. Thirty-seven distinct GEO Series involve E. coli under ciprofloxacin treatment, confirming substantial transcriptomic data availability.  
Context. This count aligns with the diverse experiment types (RNA-Seq, microarray) shown in sample records but focuses on the series-level count.  
Limitations. The geo_search tool’s default retmax does not affect total_count, but the query translation via MeSH may include synonyms; thus, some studies may be missed or over-included. GEO’s metadata do not guarantee uniform experimental designs.  
Conclusion & Future Directions. There are 37 ciprofloxacin‐related E. coli expression studies in GEO. Future analyses could extract and compare expression matrices, expand to other antibiotics, or integrate additional repositories.

References  
[1] GEO Series Search via Entrez E-utilities esearch: https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esearch.fcgi

Acknowledgments  
We acknowledge NCBI GEO and the Entrez E-utilities for data access.
